summary.headline: Q2 FY27 volume hit record 61.23 MMSCM (+12% YoY) and standalone EBITDA rose 77% to INR 47 crore, but management declined to guide Q3 margins.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue net of excise rose 29% YoY to INR 334 crore, with PAT more than doubling to INR 26 crore and PAT margin at 7.7%. EBITDA moderated sequentially from INR 62 crore in Q1 to INR 47 crore in Q2 because of higher gas sourcing costs and currency movement. A September HPHT allocation change by MoPNG temporarily cut gas availability for about a fortnight at the start of Q3, and management expects Q3 to be impacted, while still targeting roughly 15% EBITDA margin for H2. The company remains net debt-free with INR 45 crore of debt against INR 253 crore of cash and mutual funds.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: CNG volume grew 23% in H1 FY27 and now accounts for about 66% of total volume value. CNG stations rose 34% YoY to 156 and dispensing points 36% to 576.

segments.name: Commercial PNG
segments.commentary: Commercial PNG volume grew 61% in H1 FY27; commercial connections rose 48% YoY.

segments.name: Industrial PNG
segments.commentary: Industrial volumes remained weak on relative fuel economics versus alternate fuels, with sequential recovery in Q2. Industrial connections rose 8% YoY.

segments.name: Domestic PNG
segments.commentary: Domestic PNG connections rose 14% YoY. Networks: MDPE pipeline up 20% to 7,313 km; steel pipeline up 17% to 3,441 inch-km.

segments.name: Geographic mix (H1 FY27 volume)
segments.commentary: Banaskantha about 47%, Fatehgarh Sahib 33%, Namakkal and Trichy 11% (up from about 6% in FY26), Diu and Gir Somnath 9%.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at around 15%, per management in Q&A.
Q3 FY27 expected to be impacted by the temporary gas supply disruption and higher sourcing costs; Q4 expected to recover. Management declined to give rupee-per-SCM or margin guidance for Q3.
Capex for FY27 guided at INR 250-260 crore; INR 111 crore spent in H1 (INR 54 crore in Q1, INR 57 crore in Q2), with bills in line and possible overrun.
Volume growth: management said it may revise the earlier ~12% FY27 volume plan by 50-100 bps to protect margins; no expectation of exceeding prior guidance, with some moderation possible.
Sourcing tied up through 2030 via Shell India, GSPC, IOC and GAIL; management plans further long-term contracts once geopolitical volatility eases, in about six months.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex plan of INR 250-260 crore; INR 111 crore spent in H1 FY27 with bills pending.
CNG network at 156 stations and 576 dispensing points; MDPE network 7,313 km; steel pipeline 3,441 inch-km.

IPO proceeds: INR 496 crore received; INR 358.68 crore utilised by 30 Sep 2026 (INR 170.18 crore CGD network in NT area, INR 135 crore debt repayment, INR 53.50 crore general corporate purposes); about INR 137.08 crore remains for Namakkal and Tiruchirappalli network.

Namakkal and Trichy: TNSTC MoU; 83 buses converted, taking CNG fleet to 183 buses in Namakkal and 55 in Tiruchirappalli. Connectivity work started under IOC (NT) and GTN (Diu & Gir Somnath) hookup arrangements.
Two GAs (Diu & Gir Somnath, Namakkal) still in formative stage; LCNG stations and compression services provided to BPCL at Namakkal and Trichy.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 volume an all-time high of 61.23 MMSCM, +12% YoY; H1 FY27 volume 120.16 MMSCM, +10% YoY.

Gas sourcing mix in Q2 (portfolio basis): APM about 21%, new well gas about 13%, HPHT about 33%, LNG about 30%, spot 1-2% (management cited about 0.5% spot in prepared remarks). Average cost about USD 9.5/MMBtu.
Per-source cost: APM capped at USD 7/MMBtu; new well gas about USD 10.2; HPHT about USD 8.9; RLNG USD 11-12/MMBtu.
Spot gas volatile: management cited spikes to USD 29-32/MMBtu and drops to USD 19-24/MMBtu. Spot purchases to cover shortfalls raised sourcing cost.

Raw material cost rose about INR 1.2 per SCM QoQ, attributed to HPHT allocation changes, Brent-linked pricing and dollar rate movement. Price hikes passed through to consumers, with CNG kept below petrol price.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a rethink on royalty paid to promoters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with the current arrangement; royalty (2% of revenue from operations, booked in other expenses) continues until settlement, as per the IPO prospectus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and cost per MMBtu by source?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 mix: APM about 21%, NWG about 13%, HPHT about 33%, LNG about 30%, spot 1-2%. Average about USD 9.5/MMBtu; APM capped at USD 7, NWG about USD 10.2, HPHT about USD 8.9, RLNG USD 11-12.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q3 raw material cost rise and what is the HPHT impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The 3 September MoPNG HPHT methodology change favoured large players and hurt smaller ones. About 80% of the correction is done after the 19 October relaxation; the transition impact lasted about 20 days to one month. Brent and dollar movements added to costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why will Q3 not be as strong sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Brent-linked billing with GAIL, Shell and IOC uses averaged pricing that spills into later quarters; Namakkal and Trichy depend on higher-cost IOC and BPCL/GAIL short-term allocations because GAIL pipeline projects are delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company guide on Q3 margins and H2 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined rupee-per-SCM or margin guidance for Q3 given volatility, but said it remains confident of around 15% EBITDA margin for H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IRM not do a buyback given valuation below gross block?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback or promoter stake increase is not ruled out in future, but there is no such decision now; capital is focused on Namakkal and Trichy and on diversification into cleaner fuels and alternate energy.

risks_watch: Q3 FY27 margin and volume impact from HPHT allocation change and spot/short-term gas purchases; management says about 80% of the correction is done.
Brent and USD/INR movement feeding into sourcing cost; Brent-linked contracts carry averaging lags.
Industrial demand: steel rolling plants may switch back to coal or alternate fuels; NGT order implementation by Punjab Pollution Control Board pending since 26 February.
Rising other expenses (new GA start-up opex in Namakkal and Trichy) and higher depreciation as new assets are capitalised.
Capex execution against INR 250-260 crore FY27 plan; INR 137 crore of IPO proceeds still to be deployed in Namakkal and Trichy.
Net finance cost: management cited about 7-8% interest on INR 45 crore debt plus 0.5-0.6% bank guarantee charges, with H1 finance cost about INR 6 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H1 delivery and balance sheet, but cautious and non-committal on Q3 and FY27 outlook, citing gas allocation volatility, Brent, and geopolitical uncertainty. Management declined specific Q3 margin and rupee-per-SCM guidance, instead reiterating about 15% H2 EBITDA margin and a commitment to profitable, sustainable growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: HPHT allocation correction and 19 October relaxation
